title: High-end ASIC demand drives TGV adoption as TPK weighs further Taiwan expansion

summary: Persistent supply shortages have kept the niche memory market hot, with Elite Semiconductor Microelectronics Technology (ESMT) estimating that the structural supply gap exceeds 30%. The company expects tight supply and demand to continue through 2028 or longer, while price increases are set to continue in the fourth quarter of 2026 and support stronger operating performance than in the third quarter.
title: ESMT sees memory price momentum extending through 4Q26, 2027

summary: Samsung Electronics is reportedly turning to TSMC's 3nm process to produce base dies for Nvidia's custom high-bandwidth memory (NVHBM), abandoning its long-standing turnkey integration model to win a place in Nvidia's supply chain. The move could meet customer requirements, but it is raising concerns in South Korea over Samsung Foundry's competitiveness, HBM design control, and the long-term benefits of internal collaboration.
title: Samsung's Nvidia HBM bid raises four strategic concerns

summary: Russia is reportedly considering reinstating parallel imports of products from Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix to ease shortages of memory and storage devices used in data centers. However, US export controls on Russia and tight global memory supplies are expected to make it difficult for either company to resume direct shipments to the Russian market or significantly expand local sales.
title: Russia considers reinstating parallel imports of Samsung, SK Hynix products amid memory shortages

summary: Precision gearmaker Khgears International is expanding into humanoid robot joint components and expects its newly developed differential reducer to enter mass production in 2027. The company said shipments for new projects should remain strong through the fourth quarter of 2026, after reporting September revenue of NT$336 million (US$10.3 million), up 27.61% year on year.
title: Khgears targets humanoid robot joints, eyes 2027 mass production

summary: As Taiwan and the US deepen supply chain localization efforts, concrete plans for Taiwan's electrical and electronics industries to establish US industrial parks are rapidly taking shape. Minister of Economic Affairs Ming-Hsin Kung recently revealed in an interview with foreign media that Taiwan plans to collaborate with the Taiwan Electrical and Electronic Manufacturers' Association (TEEMA) to construct multiple US industrial parks. Texas has been selected as the inaugural location to help Taiwanese AI and semiconductor suppliers build a local manufacturing footprint.
title: Taiwan tech supply chain eyes Texas for first US industrial cluster

summary: With a strike by Micron Taiwan employees looming, Micron Technology said Micron Memory Taiwan and the Taichung chapter of the Taiwan Micron Memory Union had reached agreement on several issues after multiple rounds of constructive discussions. The two sides signed a labour-management agreement and agreed to withdraw the mediation scheduled for October 22. Micron will continue talks with its Taoyuan union, which has planned a one-day strike for that date.
title: Micron's Taichung union deal eases Taiwan DRAM strike risk; Taoyuan dispute remains unresolved

summary: Elon Musk's Terafab semiconductor production initiative is expanding its supplier outreach in South Korea, with Tesla and SpaceX approaching materials, components, and equipment suppliers across nearly every segment of the planned supply chain, from basic piping components and process materials to testing components.
title: Elon Musk expands South Korean supplier network for Terafab

summary: The Global Electronics Association hosted a panel titled "Component to System Integration Advances" during the IMPACT 2026 symposium, bringing together industry leaders from Unimicron, STATS ChipPAC, Wistron, and market research firm TechSearch. Covering crucial supply chain segments—including PCBs, IC substrates, OSATs, and EMS providers—the forum addressed pressing technical bottlenecks in AI-driven high-performance computing (HPC).
title: Unimicron, STATS ChipPAC, Wistron address advanced packaging bottlenecks in AI system integration

summary: Memory module maker GoldKey Technology posted record third-quarter 2026 profit, with net income topping NT$1 billion (approx. US$30.9 million) for the first time at NT$1.03 billion, up 6.2% quarter-over-quarter. However, the conversion of convertible bonds increased its share capital, pushing earnings per share down to NT$9.14 from NT$10.17 in the second quarter.
title: GoldKey Technology posts record 3Q26 profit as industrial share rises

summary: 3M Chairman and CEO Bill Brown outlined the latest progress in the company's expanded beam optics (EBO) technology during its third-quarter earnings call, highlighting a contract manufacturing agreement with Taiwan's Largan Precision and the technology's potential US$2 billion market opportunity.
title: 3M calls Largan partnership key step for US$2 billion EBO market

summary: The expansion of advanced semiconductor processes and packaging is driving demand for facility engineering, with Chi Yi Hsin Technology securing NT$4.5 billion (US$138.9 million) in orders as it joins the supply chains supporting leading foundry construction projects in Taiwan and the US. Founded in 2014, the facility engineering integrator is preparing to list on the Taipei Exchange to accelerate its entry into the capital markets.
title: 2nm and CoWoS expansion lifts Chi Yi Hsin Technology backlog to NT$4.5B

summary: Axcelis Technologies plans to break ground on a US$35 million ion implantation equipment manufacturing facility in Pyeongtaek, South Korea, expanding its semiconductor infrastructure for customers worldwide. The project highlights investment in advanced semiconductor capacity as the global economy enters the artificial intelligence era, with production scheduled to begin in 2028.
title: Axcelis plans US$35 million semiconductor facility in South Korea

summary: Samsung Electro-Mechanics has secured a KRW360.5 billion (US$271.8 million) long-term contract to supply package substrates for memory semiconductors, strengthening its position in the growing AI server component market.
title: Samsung Electro-Mechanics wins KRW360.5 billion memory substrate deal as AI demand drives expansion

summary: What began as a satellite broadband service is increasingly becoming SpaceX's platform for connecting homes, aircraft, mobile devices, and government networks.
title: Beyond broadband: SpaceX maps Starlink's expansion into aviation, mobile, next-gen capacity

summary: SpaceX has spent two decades proving that hardware once considered too complex, too capital-intensive, or too dependent on entrenched suppliers could sometimes be pulled in-house. Its Q3 earnings call suggests the company now wants to test that philosophy on perhaps the hardest manufacturing problem of all: advanced semiconductor production.
title: Analysis: From rockets to fabs, SpaceX's TeraFab bet pushes vertical integration into the semiconductor era

summary: Chinese tech giants ByteDance, Alibaba, and Tencent have collectively ordered more than 3 million units of Nvidia's new RTX PRO 5500 graphics cards, representing a total value exceeding US$35 billion, as reported by Reuters.
title: How ByteDance, Alibaba, Tencent are testing the boundaries of US AI chip restrictions

summary: Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix are upgrading their NAND flash factories in China to make chips with more than 200 layers, Reuters reported on October 21, citing four people familiar with the plans. The move would let the South Korean memory makers win back ground lost to Yangtze Memory Technologies Co (YMTC), even though US curbs on upgrading their China operations remain formally in place.
title: Samsung, SK Hynix reportedly upgrading China NAND fabs to fend off YMTC amid softening US stance

summary: Li Auto's chip and domain controller subsidiary, Mahe Xin Technology, has entered a first-round equity financing agreement worth CNY 1.625 billion (approx. US$243.33 million). The fundraising follows the automaker's recent opening of its in-house technologies to external customers, mirroring similar moves by other Chinese EV companies.
title: Li Auto chip subsidiary Mahe Xin raises CNY1.6 billion in equity financing as automakers aim to become chipmakers

summary: As Nvidia expands its chip business beyond technology giants into emerging AI markets such as new cloud providers, it has become a "central bank" helping these companies expand by backing customers and demand. But as Nvidia-backed AI cloud companies come under pressure, concerns are growing over how long Nvidia can sustain this role.
title: Nvidia becomes AI's central bank as cloud startups face mounting pressure

summary: Soaring memory prices are intensifying cost pressure across the display industry, prompting some smartphone manufacturers to downgrade panel specifications. Market estimates indicate that memory's share of flagship smartphones' bill of materials (BOM) cost is nearly six times that of displays, raising concerns that smartphone display technology could regress by about five years.
title: Memory surge drives phone makers from LTPO to LTPS

summary: Samsung Electronics has disclosed a patent application targeting GPU memory shortages when multiple users simultaneously submit requests to AI servers. By calculating data-transfer costs between GPUs and CPUs and minimizing unnecessary transfers, the technology is designed to enable AI servers to process more user requests quickly within limited memory capacity, without adding GPUs.
title: Samsung patent boosts AI server memory efficiency without adding GPUs

summary: Liquid cooling in AI data centers is moving toward more granular control architectures. Patrick Zeng, general manager of data center thermal management at Texas Instruments (TI), told DIGITIMES that as next-generation GPU computing power and rack power continue to rise, thermal management will shift from centralized control by a CDU to independent control for each server tray, a shift that will increase the use of sensors, drivers, MCUs, and other components within each rack.
title: Interview: TI sees liquid cooling shift to tray-level control in AI data centers

summary: Liquid cooling is becoming mainstream in AI servers, prompting data-center customers to assess pumps that can move 100 metric tons of water per hour as chip heat rises. Taiwan pump maker Walrus Pump expects slower ordering momentum to limit technology-pump revenue growth, while broader adoption could improve its earnings mix.
title: Walrus Pump sees slower demand for higher-capacity AI cooling pumps

summary: According to reports from Financial News , ETNews , News1 and Yonhap , Samsung Electronics' postponement of an event has intensified scrutiny of internal communications, bonus disparities, and preparations for 2027 wage talks as DX employees challenge compensation arrangements favoring the memory-focused DS division, while unions contest who should represent workers in negotiations expected to begin integrating demands in December.
title: Samsung DX division postpones meeting amid bonus tensions

summary: China's IC designers are expanding into high-speed interconnect technologies as AI inference and agent applications fuel demand for server CPUs, memory modules and connectivity chips. Montage Technology expects third-quarter 2026 profit to more than double on stronger DDR5 shipments, while Shenzhen-based Techwinsemi is developing Compute Express Link (CXL) memory expansion controllers. Together, these efforts highlight China's growing interest in AI server connectivity.
title: China's IC designers expand into AI server memory interconnects beyond DDR5

summary: Tesla recently unveiled its new Roadster, equipped with SpaceX cold-gas thruster technology, and demonstrated the vehicle hanging upside down, lifting off the ground, and performing aerial flips. The company also announced plans to begin mass production in 2028, drawing global attention to the concept of a "flying car."
title: Tesla's new Roadster opens two paths for Taiwanese suppliers, from EV components to aerospace

summary: Nvidia's lead over Huawei in China's AI accelerator market has narrowed by 80% in a year, bringing CEO Jensen Huang's warnings about losing the country's US$50 billion AI chip market closer to reality. According to IDC, Huawei shipped 572,000 Ascend chips in the first half of 2026, securing a 28% market share, just 6pp behind Nvidia, compared with a 31pp gap a year earlier.
title: Charts: Nvidia's China AI chip lead shrinks 80% as Huawei closes in

summary: LG Electronics is expanding its artificial intelligence (AI) footprint on two fronts: in-house appliance chips and GPU compute services. On one hand, the company is scaling up the deployment of custom AI chips in its home appliances to boost product differentiation. On the other hand, PADO, a startup incubated and spun off by LG NOVA (LG's North American Innovation Center), is entering the GPU compute leasing and brokerage market to explore data center opportunities.
title: LG home appliance chip volume tops 1 million; spins off startup PADO to target GPU compute leasing

summary: Elon Musk is moving ahead with Terafab, as Tesla and SpaceX reportedly negotiate with about 10 South Korean semiconductor materials, components, and equipment suppliers. The discussions cover process materials, piping and valves, wastewater recycling equipment, and semiconductor testing components, raising questions about whether Taiwan's semiconductor supply chain will benefit from the massive expansion.
title: Why Terafab approached South Korean suppliers first

summary: Taiwan's aerospace components maker Aero Win Technology is positioning itself for a new growth cycle, capitalizing on robust aircraft engine demand while expanding its role in next-generation development programs. With global aircraft production struggling to keep pace with orders, the company's gross margin reached a record 26% in the first half of 2026, up 8pp year-over-year.
title: Taiwan's Aero Win expands role in next-gen engine programs amid global aircraft backlog

summary: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi will finalize a five-year plan by the end of 2026 outlining an investment blueprint for 17 strategic sectors. The plan will prioritize semiconductors and gaming for near-term investment, while physical AI and hydrogen are positioned as the next growth drivers.
title: Japan sets execution plan for 17 growth strategies

summary: As the global foundry leader accelerates construction of advanced-process and advanced-packaging facilities in the US, semiconductor facility engineering integrator Chi Yi Hsin Technology is expanding its role in Arizona, from core facility systems and equipment hook-up to materials supply. Chi Yi Hsin Technology said its backlog reached NT$4.476 billion (US$137.5 million) as of the end of September 2026, with projects scheduled for execution through around 2028 and overall order visibility extending to 2030.
title: Chi Yi Hsin Technology's Arizona fab projects drive order backlog to NT$4.476B

summary: Samsung Electronics' foundry business will extend its 8-nanometer process, now more than eight years old, into another generation with the launch of the second-generation 8LPU+ platform in 2026. The move targets demand for automotive electronics, robots, and edge AI chips while leveraging existing deep ultraviolet (DUV) production lines to control wafer costs.
title: Samsung Foundry targets automotive, edge AI chips with 8LPU+

summary: UMC and AP Memory announced a technology and manufacturing partnership on October 22 to develop next-generation power delivery solutions for AI data centers, combining UMC's deep trench capacitor (DTC) technology and wafer manufacturing capabilities with AP Memory's silicon capacitor design and system integration expertise. The collaboration comes as rising power consumption in AI and high-performance computing (HPC) chips accelerates the shift towards near-chip power delivery and advanced packaging integration.
title: UMC, AP Memory advance AI chip power delivery with validated DTC silicon capacitors for advanced packaging

summary: Lam Research reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of US$8.2 billion, up 22% quarter-over-quarter, and forecast fourth-quarter revenue of US$8.6 billion, plus or minus US$400 million. The semiconductor equipment maker expects the wafer fabrication equipment (WFE) market to reach the mid-US$150 billion range in 2026 and initially forecasts more than US$200 billion in 2027, with percentage growth led by DRAM.
title: Lam Research sees WFE topping US$200 billion in 2027

summary: Powerchip Semiconductor Manufacturing (PSMC) reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of NT$21.3 billion (US$654.3 million), up 23% quarter-over-quarter, as higher foundry prices, a stronger average selling price (ASP) and improved capacity utilization lifted gross margin from 28% to 48% and drove net profit to NT$6.5 billion. With AI servers fueling demand for memory, power-management ICs and advanced packaging, PSMC expects double-digit revenue growth in the fourth quarter and has indicated that foundry prices will rise another 10% to 20% in 2027.
title: PSMC raises mature-node prices again, targets 20% increase in 2027

summary: Powerchip Semiconductor Manufacturing (PSMC) is urgently expanding its 3D AI foundry business and evaluating new plants in Taiwan, Singapore, and Japan, while exploring strategic joint ventures with customers. Its product portfolio includes integrated passive devices (IPDs), interposers, wafer-on-wafer (WoW) technology, and post-wafer finish (PWF) services, with demand for IPDs expected to remain visible through 2028 as AI server power consumption rises.
title: PSMC eyes Taiwan, Japan, Singapore for 3D AI foundry expansion

summary: Texas Instruments' third quarter suggested the analog chip upturn has moved beyond restocking into a broad-based recovery, and that the company's multi-year build-out of 12-inch wafer capacity is now lifting margins rather than absorbing cash. Revenue rose 28% year on year and 11% sequentially to US$6.06 billion for the quarter ended September 30, 2026.
title: Texas Instruments' analog recovery broadens as 12-inch investment turns into margin

summary: Micron does not plan to commercialize 4F² DRAM even as Chinese rival ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) advances the technology, saying the architecture offers limited benefits while adding cost and complexity.
title: Micron skips 4F² for 3D DRAM as CXMT pushes ahead

summary: US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has announced a new investment by industrial minerals company Sibelco to expand semiconductor-related manufacturing in North Carolina, as the Trump administration pushes to bring more of the chip supply chain onto US soil.
title: Sibelco to build quartz plant in North Carolina, extending US chip onshoring to raw materials

summary: Lam Research is grooming Indian companies to become its suppliers rather than relying only on its global vendor base, a senior executive said, as the US chip equipment maker deepens its presence in a market where the government now ties incentives to local sourcing.
title: Lam Research builds India supplier base to capitalize on Semicon 2.0 localization push

summary: BOS Semiconductors is partnering with LG Electronics and HANA Micron to develop and commercialize chiplet-based automotive semiconductors in South Korea, connecting domestic AI chip design with packaging and vehicle testing. ChosunBiz and ZDNet Korea reported the collaboration on October 20.
title: BOS, LG, and HANA Micron team up on Korean automotive chiplets

summary: Samsung Electronics is reportedly restructuring its semiconductor research operations and performance-based compensation system to accelerate next-generation DRAM and NAND flash development, bringing researchers and production teams closer together while addressing concerns over incentives and talent retention.
title: Samsung reportedly overhauls DRAM, NAND R&D incentives to retain talent and accelerate next-gen memory chips

summary: Intel is accelerating work on its long-delayed US semiconductor manufacturing projects, with equipment installation underway at its Fab 62 facility in Arizona and construction progressing at its Ohio site. The developments come as stronger demand for AI data center processors supports the chipmaker's efforts to expand capacity and strengthen its foundry business.
title: Intel begins Arizona Fab 62 equipment installation, advances Ohio project as AI CPU demand surges

summary: SK Hynix is reportedly working with materials and equipment suppliers to commercialise its next-generation iHBM cooling technology, targeting a reduction of more than 30% in thermal resistance. The initiative aims to address mounting heat dissipation challenges in HBM and strengthen the company's competitiveness in AI memory.
title: SK Hynix reportedly engages suppliers to bring 30% more efficient iHBM cooling to HBM5 production

summary: Texas Instruments reported strong revenue growth in its third-quarter earnings call due to strong demand across its industrial, automotive, and data center businesses. The company said it is facing a tight supply environment for its chips, but brought up its ramping of production and testing capacity, including through its new Malaysia back-end facility.
title: Texas Instruments posts rising Q3 sales across data centers, cars, industry

summary: Infineon Technologies is expanding its work with Nvidia on 800-volt direct current power architectures for AI data centers, with a focus on gallium nitride (GaN) chips in the intermediate bus converter (IBC), the company said on October 21.
title: Infineon, Nvidia push gallium nitride power for 800-volt AI data centers

summary: China's Advanced Micro-Fabrication Equipment (AMEC) has shipped the first unit of its Primo Domingo high-selectivity vapor-phase etching system to a major domestic semiconductor research and manufacturing customer, marking a step forward in China's efforts to develop indigenous equipment for next-generation 3D chips.
title: AMEC ships first Primo Domingo selective etching system, targeting critical gaps in China's advanced 3D chipmaking

summary: Highlighting the deepening industrial synergies between Europe and Asia, the Egis Group TechDay Taiwan-France Strategic CPU Partnership Signing Ceremony hosted the official signing between Egis Group and SiPearl. The landmark ceremony unveiled a joint initiative to build a Mobius 100 CPU and UCIe chiplet-based marketplace, establishing a cooperative framework for sovereign AI and high-performance computing (HPC) data center infrastructure.
title: Taiwan-France semiconductor alliance strengthens with CPU pact between SiPearl and Egis Group

summary: Magnate Technology expects rising aircraft engine demand and semiconductor equipment opportunities to support growth as it expands production capacity, with implications for global aviation and chip supply chains. The aerospace components maker forecasts revenue of nearly NT$2 billion (US$61.5 million) in 2026 and expects 15% to 20% revenue growth in 2027.
title: Magnate Technology sees aerospace, semiconductor growth opportunities

summary: TSMC is scouting Texas for possible new US capacity, even as it builds out its advanced-process fabs in Arizona. Chairman C.C. Wei confirmed that a team has been sent to Texas to assess expansion opportunities. TSMC is also discussing cooperation with Elon Musk's Terafab, on the condition that it keeps operational control. Together, the moves could shift TSMC's US strategy from expanding existing sites to choosing new locations and exploring capacity partnerships.
title: Why is TSMC suddenly looking at Texas?

summary: Invasive brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) are demonstrating long-term commercial potential. Neuralink has enabled paralysed patients to control computers and robotic arms through thought; Synchron's iOS integration lets patients operate iPads; and Science combines implanted chips with smart glasses to help visually impaired patients recognise text again. Potential applications extend to unmanned vehicles and defence.
title: DIGITIMES Insight: BCI grasping reaches market; implant stability and chip heat keep advanced uses beyond 2030

summary: AI-driven growth will push the semiconductor industry past the US$1.6 trillion mark in 2026, while accelerating chip development cycles to one new product every nine months, Etron Chairman Nicky Lu said. He warned that the next 3 to 5 years will be critical for Taiwan, which risks facing intense competition unless it builds stronger software, system, and architecture advantages.
title: AI cuts chip R&D cycles to 9 months, says Etron chair

summary: Texas Instruments (TI) held its latest earnings call this week, projecting fourth-quarter 2026 revenue of US$5.8 billion to US$6.3 billion. The midpoint of its guidance is broadly in line with third-quarter revenue, outperforming the seasonal declines typically seen in the fourth quarter.
title: Texas Instruments sees up to $1,000 in chip content per humanoid robot as analog supply tightens

summary: Mitsubishi Electric has announced plans to carve out its distribution panel components business for factories and commercial buildings into a joint venture (JV) with Swiss power and automation giant ABB. Mitsubishi Electric will spin off the division and transfer a 51% stake to ABB. Moving forward, the Japanese conglomerate will focus on data center infrastructure and high-voltage grid applications positioned further upstream in power transmission and distribution.
title: Mitsubishi Electric, ABB form joint venture for power distribution business

summary: Tesla and Nvidia are reportedly investing a combined KRW3.7 trillion (US$2.8 billion) to help Samsung Electro-Mechanics expand Ajinomoto Build-up Film (ABF) substrate production facilities in South Korea. The move reflects growing efforts by global technology companies to secure stable supplies of high-performance semiconductor substrates for AI applications.
title: Tesla, Nvidia reportedly invest KRW3.7 trillion to secure Samsung Electro-Mechanics ABF capacity

summary: Rapidus chairman Tetsuro Higashi said the Japanese chipmaker remains broadly on track to begin mass production of 2nm chips in the second half of 2027. Winning customers remains a key challenge, and initial demand is expected to come mainly from the United States, where demand related to artificial intelligence is strong.
title: Rapidus courts US AI customers ahead of planned 2H27 2nm mass production

summary: Japan's Leading-edge Semiconductor Technology Center (LSTC), Hokkaido University, Fujifilm Corporation, GE HealthCare Japan, and imec announced a joint initiative in Tokyo on October 20 to develop a next-generation medical imaging system powered by a dedicated 2nm AI inference chip. The initiative aims to dramatically accelerate image processing efficiency and enable real-time computing directly on medical equipment.
title: Japan targets 2nm medical AI chip with IBM design, Rapidus eyed for foundry

summary: The US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) has banned two electronic devices from entering the US market because both contain surveillance chips made by Huawei's HiSilicon. The move marks the first time the FCC has used a new rule targeting devices whose chipmakers are deemed national security risks.
title: First chip-level device on the list: US FCC bans two devices with Huawei HiSilicon chips under new rule

summary: In the era of AI and high-performance computing (HPC), the once-separate worlds of chip design, packaging, and circuit boards are converging. According to the Global Electronics Association, AI server motherboards have become the largest, thickest, and most structurally complex PCBs ever manufactured, drawing substrate and PCB makers, which historically reacted to decisions made by chipmakers and packaging clients, into the heart of AI hardware development.
title: Interview: From afterthought to bottleneck, circuit boards move to the heart of AI hardware

summary: Following TSMC's third-quarter 2026 earnings call, DIGITIMES analyst Luke Lin provided in a podcast additional analysis of several details that received limited attention in market coverage, including a new 3nm fab at the Southern Taiwan Science Park (STSP), the transfer of Nvidia-related high-bandwidth memory (HBM) base die orders to TSMC, and whether demand for A14 includes Intel server CPUs.
title: Podcast highlights: TSMC's 3nm demand story, Samsung HBM shift, and A14 ramp

summary: Taiwan's first-ever strike in the semiconductor industry has temporarily drawn to a close. A 24-hour warning strike spearheaded by Micron Technology's Taoyuan union concluded on the morning of October 23, 2026. During the action, an internal ballot saw nearly 70% of all union members sign statements opposing management's proposed compensation structure. Formal labor-management negotiations are set to resume on October 27.
title: Taiwan's inaugural semiconductor strike pauses as nearly 70% of Micron Taoyuan Union rejects new bonus offer

summary: Nvidia has unveiled a prototype of its next-generation co-packaged optics (CPO) technology, Optics-on-Interposer (OOI), at SEMICON West 2026. The design moves the optical engine from a conventional organic package substrate to the silicon interposer carrying the compute chips, increasing bandwidth density and reducing power consumption for future AI system interconnects.
title: Nvidia unveils OOI CPO prototype for post-2028 AI needs

summary: Hermes Testing Solutions Inc. (HTSI), a semiconductor wafer-testing solutions provider, is expanding its Taiwan operations. Its board approved budget authorisations on October 22 for a new R&D centre in Hsinchu and a manufacturing centre in south-central Taiwan, with total investment expected to exceed NT$7 billion (approx. US$215 million).
title: Taiwan wafer-testing supplier Hermes Testing Solutions commits more than US$215 million to advanced chip testing expansion

summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said the company did not expect memory supply to exceed demand in the coming years and remained open to working with China's ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT). The comments, made during the GTC Berlin conference and reported by CNBC, came as falling market valuations for memory manufacturers and new Chinese dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) developments intensified concerns about oversupply.
title: Nvidia rejects near-term memory glut fears, leaves CXMT cooperation open

summary: The US Department of Commerce has signed letters of intent with four companies to provide up to US$389 million in federal research and development awards under the CHIPS and Science Act, targeting the semiconductors and materials used to control, convert, and deliver power. The department announced the agreements on October 22, 2026.
title: US signs up to US$389 million in CHIPS R&D deals for power chips and fusion

summary: LG Display (LGD) returned to an operating profit in the third quarter of 2026, showing how far its OLED shift now drives earnings, and how little room it leaves when currency and component costs turn against it. Operating profit was KRW250.6 billion (approx. US$188.96 million), compared with a loss in the second quarter, on revenue of KRW6.28 trillion, up 12% from the previous quarter but down 10% from a year earlier, according to the company's preliminary filing on October 22.
title: LG Display returns to profit as OLED mix offsets chipflation drag

summary: Samsung Electro-Mechanics (Semco) is gaining pricing power as AI server demand extends multilayer ceramic capacitor (MLCC) lead times beyond a year. Shortages now span consumer, automotive and industrial products, prompting customers to secure 2027 supplies.
title: Semco's 61-week MLCC lead times give suppliers upper hand in AI supply chain

summary: Western Digital argues that demand for hard drives depends less on the current wave of AI spending than investors fear. On its fiscal first-quarter earnings call on October 22, the company said demand for disk storage now comes from four separate sources: cloud services, model training, inference and AI agents, and physical AI. Each, it said, could offset weakness in the others. The company is also trying to move hard drives into faster AI workloads that are currently served by flash memory.
title: Western Digital argues AI's longer payoff lies in stored data, not compute

summary: Huawei Technologies has secured a seven-year, CNY15 billion (approx. US$2.3 billion) offshore yuan loan from six Chinese banks, as rising research spending and memory costs weigh on its cash flow. The financing, arranged by domestic lenders, is Huawei's first offshore syndicated borrowing since 2020, Bloomberg reported, citing a person familiar with the matter.
title: Mounting R&D and memory costs push Huawei to borrow US$2.3B from six Chinese banks

summary: India's tech push opens markets unevenly: foreign suppliers get first crack at Tata's fab, Lam courts local vendors, Jio's IPO tests its 5G pitch, and CleanMax powers AI data centers.
title: India roundup: India's tech build-out opens new markets, but foreign suppliers are first in line

summary: Taiwan doesn't stop often. On Friday, October 23, Typhoon Champi made it stop.
title: Taiwan sits out global chip selloff, thanks to typhoon

summary: The world's largest contract chipmaker is weighing whether the motors inside its factory-automation equipment can run without rare-earth magnets, a sign that China's grip on rare earths now reaches the machinery that keeps fabs running, just as a key Chinese export-control pause approaches its legal expiry date.
title: TSMC reportedly surveys suppliers on rare-earth-free motors as China's export-control pause nears legal expiry

summary: The US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) granted Intel a waiver to its ban on foreign-made mobile robots, which will allow it to update its fleet of autonomous guided vehicles (AGVs). Intel had earlier petitioned the agency for an exemption, saying that not doing so would threaten chip production in the country.
title: FCC grants Intel a waiver to foreign robot ban to prevent chip disruptions

summary: Samsung Electronics has ordered additional equipment to fill the remaining space at its first foundry fab in Taylor, Texas, a move that would lift the plant's 2nm capacity to 20,000 wafers per month in the second half of 2027, ZDNet Korea reported on October 23, citing industry sources.
title: Samsung reportedly orders final tools for first Taylor fab as Texas site nears 2nm output cap

summary: Israeli security firm Lava identified 32 Nvidia Blackwell Ultra B300 GPUs through monitoring endpoints linked to China Telecom, a state-owned carrier. The chips are barred from sale to China under US export controls. The finding adds to questions about whether the restrictions can keep advanced AI processors out of the country, but the network data does not establish where the GPUs are physically located.
title: Nvidia B300 chips reportedly surface on China Telecom-linked network, raising export-control questions

summary: Doosan Robotics is focusing its sales efforts on large automotive and semiconductor manufacturers as it develops AI-powered systems capable of handling more complex factory tasks, Hyeonchang Jeon, senior manager of the company's Korea sales team, said in an interview with DIGITIMES at FIX 2026 in Daegu, South Korea.
title: Doosan Robotics targets automakers, chipmakers as Chinese rivals cut prices

summary: The claim that more than half of China's artificial intelligence (AI) computing power is being used to produce micro-dramas has reignited debate in China's technology sector over whether the country is directing too much of its AI computing resources to entertainment content while neglecting productivity applications.
title: ByteDance denies AI micro-dramas consume over half of China's AI computing power

summary: South Korean autonomous delivery company NT1 plans to begin assembling Chinese-designed delivery vans locally in 2027, gradually adding Korean-made components as it seeks approval to operate the vehicles on public roads.
title: NT1 plans to assemble Chinese delivery vans in Korea in 2027

summary: South Korean optics maker Optoelec is seeing growing interest from AI data center customers as it seeks to expand its wafer-level optics (WLO) business into high-speed optical communications, a market where Taiwanese suppliers are already moving toward commercial production.
title: OPTOELEC seeks AI data center orders as Himax advances CPO optics

summary: Geothermal energy commercialization in Taiwan has taken a major step forward with a 20-plus MW corporate power purchase agreement (CPPA) from a semiconductor giant, yet for geothermal energy developers and operators, numerous obstacles still remain before it can become a stable, continuous power source.
title: For Taiwan's geothermal sector, institutional barriers outweigh drilling challenges

summary: India's semiconductor drive has largely been led by New Delhi, which selects projects for large central incentives while state governments add their own packages of land, infrastructure and financial support. Tamil Nadu is now giving semiconductor investors another route.
title: Tamil Nadu adds independent chip subsidy route as Indian states vie for investment

summary: This week's coverage highlights shifting technology supply chains and rising demand across foldable smartphones, memory, energy storage, robotics, and AI infrastructure. Apple lifted its iPhone Duo shipment target after strong preorders, while memory makers faced conflicting forecasts over Chinese capacity and sustained AI demand. Taiwan advanced industrial microgrids and saw its first semiconductor strike, as Texas Instruments reported tightening analog supply. Chinese energy storage suppliers reportedly retreated from the US amid reciprocal technology and ownership restrictions.
title: Weekly news roundup: iPhone Duo shipment target revised upward amid display issues

summary: China’s semiconductor and electronics supply chains are reporting a wave of price increases, from Goke Microelectronics raising quotes for hybrid-packaged memory products to Hygon considering higher CPU and deep computing unit (DCU) prices. The moves reflect rising costs for raw materials, components, and upstream supplies, but whether they can help China escape deflationary pressure remains uncertain.
title: China supply-chain price hikes strain domestic demand

summary: AWS has launched the open-source TorchNeuron tool, allowing developers to port PyTorch artificial intelligence (AI) applications to its custom Trainium chips without rewriting code. Google has followed with TorchTPU, while AMD and Intel are integrating AI software optimizations as chipmakers challenge Nvidia's market advantage built on the CUDA ecosystem.
title: AWS, Google challenge CUDA as AMD, Intel cut AI switch costs

summary: Fujifilm Electronic Materials is expanding its advanced semiconductor materials footprint in South Korea by increasing extreme ultraviolet (EUV) photoresist capacity in Pyeongtaek and expanding chemical mechanical polishing (CMP) slurry production in Cheonan. The investments will deepen local support for customers including Samsung Electronics as AI and advanced-process demand grows.
title: Fujifilm expands South Korean capacity to meet AI chip demand

summary: More than half of China's AI token usage is reportedly concentrated in short dramas and video generation, but ByteDance's Doubao has disputed the figure, saying video-generation models account for only about 10% of overall computing resources. The conflicting estimates highlight the difficulty of assessing AI compute consumption and its commercial value.
title: China AI token debate highlights challenge of monetizing compute

summary: US materials giant 3M recently entered into a strategic partnership with Taiwanese optical component manufacturer Genius Electronic Optical (GSEO), with plans to acquire a 4.7% stake in the company through a private placement. The two companies aim to accelerate technology development and expand manufacturing capacity for expanded beam optics (EBO).
title: Analysis: 3M's investment in Genius Electronic Optical puts EBO mass production to the test

summary: DRAM price growth has slowed sharply in the fourth quarter of 2026, but severe supply shortages are intensifying as manufacturers continue to restrict shipments. Industry sources expect DRAM supply from leading manufacturers to shrink by 30% to 50% for the next two to three quarters, widening the supply gap in 2027.
title: DRAM price gains fall short as supply shrinks up to 50%

summary: Fine M-Tec has rejected claims that components it supplied contributed to reported display damage in Apple's first foldable iPhone, saying the issue involves multiple components and precision mechanisms. The dispute could affect perceptions of the South Korean supplier even as analysts forecast growth from expanding foldable device demand ahead.
title: Fine M-Tec rejects component blame as foldable market outlook remains positive

summary: The rapid expansion of AI data centers is driving demand beyond GPUs, memory chips, and advanced packaging. As power consumption in GPU clusters rises, data centers need not only more chips but also more efficient power delivery systems. Power plants and electrical grids outside data centers are also under pressure to close supply gaps, potentially tightening power semiconductor supplies and spreading shortages to other applications.
title: AI data center boom risks squeezing power chip supplies for auto, electronics

summary: Major package substrate makers, including Samsung Electro-Mechanics (Semco), are concentrating capital spending on large, high-layer-count ABF substrates, while capacity expansion for BT substrates used in memory packaging remains limited. With BT substrate supply tightening and demand for low-power SOCAMM memory modules rising, South Korea's Simmtech could benefit from its business in both memory package substrates and module PCBs.
title: Simmtech steps up SOCAMM investment as BT substrate supply tightens

summary: AMD and Nvidia have separately invested in supply-chain capacity expansion, making substrates, packaging, and testing key priorities as AI demand diversifies. The moves show that chipmakers are extending competition beyond performance and architecture design to control over critical manufacturing resources.
title: AMD, Nvidia target substrate capacity amid 4x expansion constraints

summary: Expanding investment in AI data centers is putting pressure on memory supply and demand across the automotive industry. As semiconductor companies prioritize high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and server products, automotive memory faces rising prices and tighter supplies, making automakers' direct procurement, long-term partnerships, and in-house chip design increasingly strategic.
title: AI demand squeezes automotive memory, pushing automakers to take control of chip supply

summary: AI is driving a steady upward revision in chip demand, but semiconductor equipment shortages are not the biggest obstacle to expanding AI chip production, according to industry sources. Instead, talent shortages, factory construction constraints, materials availability, power infrastructure, and funding are emerging as more serious challenges, particularly in the US.
title: Semiconductor equipment is not AI chip growth's biggest bottleneck

summary: Chinese AI chipmaker Cambricon Technologies reported a 131.49% increase in net profit attributable to shareholders for the first nine months of 2026, while revenue more than doubled. Third-quarter net profit rose nearly 150% from a year earlier.
title: Cambricon profit jumps 131%, CEO says firm never gave 1 million-chip forecast

summary: One of the world's three major machine tool shows, Japan's International Machine Tool Fair (JIMTOF 2026), opened this week, with 94 Taiwan companies exhibiting. The exhibitors are showcasing precision machining, key components and smart automation while deepening manufacturing supply-chain cooperation between Taiwan and Japan.
title: JIMTOF 2026 draws 94 Taiwan machine tool exhibitors

summary: South Korean memory module substrate maker TLB has begun developing substrates for SOCAMM3, a next-generation low-power memory module for AI servers, with two major memory customers at home and abroad, according to sources. The company expects SOCAMM3 to enter mass production in 2028 as it expands SOCAMM2 production and builds capacity to retain its position in the high-end memory module substrate market.
title: TLB develops SOCAMM3 substrates; Vietnam plant to break ground

summary: China-based IC design firm Goke Microelectronics will raise prices for its Known Good Die (KGD) packaged products by US$0.5 to US$1.5 per unit from November 2026, depending on capacity. The move marks the second price adjustment known to customers in 2026, as AI-driven memory demand keeps double data rate (DDR) memory supplies tight and pressure spreads to niche memory and integrated packaging products.
title: Goke Microelectronics raises KGD packaging prices again

summary: South Korean semiconductor equipment component maker MiCo Ceramics is set to acquire an idle facility in Gumi, North Gyeongsang Province, from LG Display (LGD) for KRW150 billion (approx. US$113.2 million). The acquisition of the land and buildings will allow MiCo Ceramics to expand production capacity for key products, including ceramic heaters and electrostatic chucks (ESCs). The deal highlights a broader trend across the tech sector, as real estate assets shed during display industry downsizing are repurposed for the semiconductor supply chain.
title: MiCo Ceramics acquires idle LGD plant for KRW150 billion to boost semiconductor component capacity

summary: Silicon Valley venture capital firm Playground Global has returned to Taiwan alongside a cohort of portfolio companies specializing in memory, power management, optical communications, and advanced packaging to showcase joint technical breakthroughs and commercial strategies. The firm is also hosting an executive dinner with Foxconn Chairman Young Liu, highlighting their deep-seated partnership and ongoing commitment to Taiwan's technology ecosystem.
title: Pat Gelsinger warns AI compute efficiency must jump 10,000x amid power, memory, and fab constraints

summary: China's CXMT has reportedly declined Apple's inquiry about purchasing DRAM, prioritizing supply to domestic customers instead. As global memory supplies tighten and prices rise, the Chinese memory maker's capacity allocation and companies' efforts to secure supply have drawn attention.
title: CXMT reportedly prioritizes China demand, rejecting Apple's DRAM inquiry

summary: Taiwanese startup Skymizer has formally announced a strategic partnership with Egis Technology to develop Flow (T12), a new-generation AI inference chip. Fabricated on TSMC's 12nm node and paired with LPDDR5 memory, the solution requires just three PCIe cards and 750W of power to run 3-trillion-parameter large language models (LLMs). This represents roughly one-tenth the power consumption of a comparable Nvidia H100 deployment.
title: Skymizer partners with Egis to develop 12nm and 6nm AI accelerators

summary: Silicon Valley venture capital firm Playground Global returned to Taiwan with six portfolio companies spanning memory, power management, optical communications and advanced packaging, showcasing technology breakthroughs and expansion plans aimed at easing AI computing bottlenecks. Its newest portfolio companies also made their Taiwan debut.
title: From superconductors to optics: The six Silicon Valley startups bringing AI bottleneck solutions to Taiwan

summary: SK Hynix is looking beyond its position as a leading supplier of high-bandwidth memory (HBM), using venture investments to gain a greater say in how next-generation AI infrastructure is designed.
title: SK Hynix's next bet goes beyond memory chips

summary: Memory maker Macronix International set a new quarterly record in the third quarter of 2026, with gross margin reaching 70.5% and net profit after tax totaling NT$109.5 billion (approx. US$3.37 billion). Chairman Min-chiu Wu said future growth will come mainly from price increases, as limited existing capacity and investment lead times of more than one year prevent rapid expansion through capacity additions.
title: Macronix posts record 3Q26 profit as gross margin hits 70%

summary: HCLTech and Japan's Rapidus have inaugurated development centers in Bengaluru and Hubli, India, expanding their semiconductor engineering collaboration across Asia. The facilities will support advanced chip work, while a planned talent pipeline could connect Indian engineers with Rapidus' manufacturing ambitions in Japan, highlighting the cross-border partnerships shaping semiconductor supply chains.
title: HCLTech and Rapidus open India centers to support semiconductor engineering

summary: Cadence Design Systems' third quarter suggests demand for chip design tools is still rising, with AI-driven design work showing up in both revenue and backlog, while the cost of buying growth is hurting profitability. Revenue for the three months ended September 30, 2026, rose 22% from a year earlier, the company said on October 26, but operating income barely moved.
title: Cadence raises 2026 outlook as AI design demand drives record backlog

summary: Cadence Design Systems used its third-quarter earnings call to argue that demand for chip design tools is no longer tied only to the AI hardware buildout. It pointed to analog and memory chipmakers, system companies, and new entrants such as space and finance firms designing their own silicon. Analysts on the October 26 call pressed two questions that will shape the coming year: how much growth comes from agentic AI rather than hardware, and whether Cadence can match the long-term targets rival Synopsys set a month earlier.
title: Cadence says chip design demand is broadening beyond AI as analysts test margins, rival targets

summary: Cadence Design Systems is betting that chipmakers will want AI models trained on its own design tools and run wherever customers choose. That puts it on a different route from rival Synopsys, which is building its specialized model with OpenAI on OpenAI-hosted infrastructure. On October 26, alongside its third-quarter results, Cadence introduced Maestro, a portfolio of domain-specialized AI models that power its AI super agents for chip and system design.
title: Cadence bets on its own chip design AI models as Synopsys teams up with OpenAI

summary: India's smartphone shipments fell 20% year over year in the third quarter of 2026, reaching a decade low as higher memory costs pushed device prices up. The downturn highlights affordability pressures for consumers and could prompt manufacturers to raise prices, reshape portfolios, and rely on premium segments globally.
title: India's smartphone shipments hit a decade low in 3Q26 amid rising prices

summary: Vietnam's first wafer fab may miss its 2027 trial-production target, Reuters reported on October 26, citing concerns about project execution and equipment procurement. Developer Viettel, however, says the project remains on schedule.
title: Vietnam's first fab reportedly faces doubts over 2027 target

summary: In its preliminary IPO registration statement filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission, Anthropic describes how much of its capacity depends on a small group of chip and memory suppliers, most of them in East Asia.
title: Anthropic's IPO filing puts TSMC, HBM, direct leasing at the center of AI compute risk

summary: Intel has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Classiq, a quantum computing software company, in a move aimed at combining Classiq's quantum algorithm synthesis platform with Intel's silicon-based quantum hardware and semiconductor manufacturing capabilities.
title: Intel to acquire quantum computing software firm Classiq

summary: Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix are targeting the second quarter of 2027 to begin volume shipments of eight-layer HBM4 memory to Nvidia, ZDNet Korea reported on October 26, as the AI chipmaker reassesses its memory strategy for next-generation Rubin Ultra accelerators.
title: Samsung, SK Hynix eye 2Q27 shipments of 8-layer HBM4 to Nvidia

summary: Applied Materials plans to increase its stake in Dutch semiconductor equipment maker BE Semiconductor Industries (Besi) to approximately 20% from 9%, deepening its involvement in advanced chip packaging as demand for hybrid-bonding equipment accelerates.
title: Applied Materials to raise Besi stake to 20% as hybrid-bonding orders surge

summary: As military conflict in the Middle East cripples global energy infrastructure, the United States is emerging as the critical anchor for the world's high-tech manufacturing sector. Amid a historic supply crisis for helium, an indispensable element in the production of semiconductors and advanced electronics, as well as in medical imaging, the US Department of Energy has officially designated helium as a critical material under the Energy Act of 2020.
title: US designates helium as critical material amid Middle East supply shock

summary: South Korean memory chip designer Jeju Semiconductor is struggling to secure enough wafer capacity from Taiwan's Powerchip Semiconductor Manufacturing (PSMC), limiting its sales growth as strong memory demand drives up prices and manufacturing costs.
title: PSMC capacity crunch holds back Jeju Semiconductor's growth

summary: Broadcom has reached a deal with several financial firms for them to finance the purchase of US$63 billion worth of its chips for Anthropic. The agreement highlights how the line between supplier and lender is becoming blurred among some chipmakers, as well as Wall Street's growing involvement in funding arrangements as AI infrastructure spending continues to expand.
title: Broadcom, financial firms agree on US$63 billion funding for Anthropic chip purchases

summary: The momentum surrounding chip financing is being met with a subtler but increasingly consequential shift in how AI infrastructure is funded, as technology giants expand compute commitments through long-duration financing structures rather than relying solely on outright equipment purchases.
title: SpaceX turns Nvidia GPUs into long-duration assets with US$40 billion Apollo deal

summary: Kentec, a subsidiary of Kenmec Group, is shifting beyond its traditional role as a contract manufacturer of components to become a systems integration provider (SIP) for complete AI data center (AIDC) infrastructure. title: Kentec targets CSP opportunities with AIDC infrastructure integration

summary: Asus and Intel on October 27 unveiled the new commercial laptop Asus ExpertBook A7 in Taiwan, as on-premises AI computing devices gain attention from enterprises and creators alongside traditional business PCs. Asus said products related to Nvidia RTX Spark, particularly models with 64GB and 128GB of memory, are being allocated due to strong global demand, with the next shipments expected to arrive progressively by the end of October.
title: Cloud AI costs drive demand for on-premises computing, squeezing Asus RTX Spark supply

summary: Asus expects commercial PC prices in Taiwan to rise nearly 10% in the second half of 2026 after surging almost 30% in the first half, as higher memory and processor costs continue to pressure the PC supply chain. The company forecasts that enterprise PC demand, AI edge-computing applications, and replacement cycles will drive simultaneous growth in commercial PC volumes and prices in 2027.
title: Asus sees commercial PC prices rising nearly 10% in 2H26

summary: Micron Technology is heading to South Korea to recruit engineers for its Taiwan operations, with interviews scheduled in Seoul in late November, as a bonus dispute at its Taoyuan plant remains unresolved. The company and the Taoyuan union held a second round of negotiations on October 27 without reaching an agreement, and a third round has been tentatively set for November 6. At the same time, Micron is advancing a global compensation overhaul, reflecting how profit sharing and competition for technical talent have become a focus for the industry as AI memory demand expands.
title: Micron recruits in South Korea for Taiwan roles as Taoyuan strike dispute persists

summary: Anthropic recently disclosed details of its computing partnerships with Google, Amazon Web Services (AWS), Microsoft, Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), and other providers in its S-1 filing for an initial public offering (IPO), revealing distinct cooperation models and chip technologies across its partner ecosystem.
title: Anthropic's surging compute demand fuels ASIC prospects, favoring Broadcom over MediaTek

summary: US AI startup Anthropic has formally filed for an initial public offering (IPO) with the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), identifying competitive pressure from Chinese AI companies, model distillation, and cross-border technology restrictions among its operational risks.
title: Anthropic's IPO filing highlights China AI rivalry as model distillation, chip export controls emerge as key risks

summary: Elon Musk recently confirmed the possibility of a merger between SpaceX and Tesla, signaling an ambition to redefine competition in the AI era beyond individual products and technological advantages toward integration across the entire industrial value chain, encompassing semiconductors, energy, computing, communications, and autonomous systems.
title: Analysis: SpaceX–Tesla merger could reshape AI industry integration, capital allocation, US-China tech rivalry

summary: Unimicron Technology is reshaping its global production footprint and steering resources toward Taiwan's higher-margin AI supply chain as surging AI and high-performance computing (HPC) chip demand drives the need for high-layer-count, large-size IC substrates. title: Unimicron steers resources to Taiwan AI substrates with NT$50.9B equipment orders, Japan unit sale

summary: Chunghwa Precision Test Tech (CHPT), a major semiconductor test interface supplier, posted record revenue and profit in the third quarter of 2026 as consolidated net profit reached NT$551 million (US$16.97 million), up 11.5% quarter on quarter and double the figure from a year earlier. The company has earned more than one times its paid-in capital for three consecutive quarters, with earnings per share reaching NT$16.75.
title: CHPT posts record 3Q26 results as nine-month profit jumps over 90%

summary: Toyota Motor Corporation is accelerating the commercialization of robots, creating potential opportunities for Ikka Holdings (IKKA-KY) to leverage its existing Japanese automotive supply-chain relationships and compete for robot component orders. IKKA, a long-standing supplier of Toyota-related automotive products, also plans to strengthen its metal-gear and robotic-arm assembly capabilities through an investment in Yijin Precision, extending its customer relationships into new applications.
title: Toyota accelerates robot commercialization as IKKA targets supply-chain opportunities

summary: Rising demand for high-end AI chips is accelerating Powertech's transformation into an advanced packaging strategic partner. Powertech said its utilization rate exceeded 90% in the third quarter of 2026 and is expected to rise further in the fourth quarter as revenue grows, putting the company on track for record annual revenue.

summary: Taiwan directs too much public research and development (R&D) funding to its national research institutes, according to Chenming Hu, a former chief technology officer of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC). In his new book, Find the Solutions , Hu argues that this funding does not achieve the same multiplier effect as investment in universities.
title: Ex-TSMC CTO says Taiwan's research institutes get too much funding and train too little talent

summary: Surging demand for AI computing is driving advanced packaging toward larger form factors, according to Ting-Hao Lin, R&D vice president at Kinsus Interconnect Technology, speaking at the 2026 TPCA Show. To support this trend, substrate materials must deliver low warpage and exceptional dimensional stability while overcoming challenges in thermal expansion mismatches and structural stress.
title: DIGITIMES Insight: Kinsus Tech identifies three challenges for larger AI chip packages

summary: Huawei has extended its semiconductor-focused "Tau (τ) Law" framework to 5G base station design, using co-design across algorithms, chip architectures, and high-speed interconnects to boost baseband processing efficiency and enhance the wireless user experience. The company unveiled its OSCAR intelligent channel-processing solution, its next-generation UBBPi baseband series, and the VitaAAU active antenna unit for the U6GHz band, with the VitaAAU already entering commercial deployment in select overseas markets.
title: Huawei deploys Tau Law in base-station design, rolling out new wireless baseband overseas

summary: The global memory shortage is no longer lifting only the commodity DRAM giants. title: Niche memory price rally lifts Ingenic's third-quarter profit 2,595%

summary: The global notebook market faces steep cost increases for key components including memory and processors, but Asus is keeping annual shipments relatively stable through its commercial PC and high-value product strategies. title: Asus notebook shipments hold steady as commercial PCs offset gaming decline

summary: As Elon Musk predicts that more than 200 new cloud providers, or neoclouds, face impending bankruptcy or acquisition in a global market consolidation, a new report from Frost & Sullivan and LeadLeo Research indicates that SenseTime Group secured nearly half of China's neocloud market in the first half of 2026. The market share was captured primarily through its AI infrastructure platform, SenseCore.
title: SenseCore captures nearly half of China's neocloud market as heterogeneous chips boost compute efficiency

Instead, Macronix will allocate more than NT$30 billion (US$925 million) in capital expenditure toward embedded MultiMediaCard (eMMC) and NAND Flash. The initial phase of new capacity is expected to ramp up gradually from the second half of 2027 through year-end. "As long as we target th
title: Macronix halts NOR expansion, phases out ROM, bets NT$30B expansion on eMMC NAND

summary: Taiwan-based Phison Electronics received two awards at Micron Supplier Day 2026, marking the third consecutive year the company has earned recognition from the US memory chipmaker.
title: Phison wins Micron supplier awards for third straight year

summary: United Microelectronics (UMC) saw operating momentum strengthen in the third quarter of 2026, as demand for artificial intelligence (AI), high-performance computing (HPC), communications, and automotive chips continued to drive the mature and specialty process markets.
title: UMC utilization tops 90% in 2H26 as AI demand drives expansion

summary: Applications for silicon carbide (SiC) and gallium nitride (GaN) power devices are expanding across the electronics industry, affecting not only component selection but also product design, manufacturing capabilities and supply chain planning, according to new research from the Global Electronics Association and Accuris, an engineering intelligence and electronic component data provider.

summary: Memory module maker Team Group reported record third-quarter results for 2026, with earnings per share soaring 1,482.55% year-over-year, while its board approved plans for a new plant in New Taipei City that is scheduled to begin production in the second quarter of 2027 and increase total capacity by about 50%.
title: Team Group earnings per share surges 1,483% in 3Q26 as new plant targets 50% capacity boost

summary: Lenovo Group announced that its annual global innovation event, Tech World, will return to CES 2027 in Las Vegas, taking place at Sphere as part of the keynote program. The event will feature a lineup of prominent speakers and showcase the latest technological innovations and achievements, while combining technology and music to deliver a unique, immersive experience.
title: Lenovo previews CES 2027 lineup focused on AI agents, hybrid AI

Early coverage described the two Macs as modest chip upgrades and the iPad mini as a substantial redesign that now costs more.

title: SK Hynix's record quarter shows AI demand turning memory into a contracted, supply-limited business

title: NXP's automotive content gains, industrial demand strengthen its growth outlook

summary: NXP Semiconductors is heading into 2027 with management arguing that its growth now rests on several structural drivers rather than a cyclical rebound. title: NXP lines up software-defined vehicles, industrial AI and data centers for double-digit growth in 2027

summary: SK Hynix is reassessing how to finance the US manufacturing expansion of its NAND flash subsidiary Solidigm after shelving a potential initial public offering (IPO), as the South Korean memory maker prepares for higher capital spending in 2027 while committing approximately KRW100 trillion to shareholder returns this year.
title: SK Hynix looks beyond IPO to fund Solidigm's US expansion

summary: SK Hynix is turning to high-bandwidth flash (HBF) to address growing memory bottlenecks in AI inference, as increasingly complex AI agents generate more data than can be economically stored in high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and DRAM alone.
title: SK Hynix's next AI memory bet isn't HBM

summary: AMD is backing one of its largest AI customers with capital and chips. title: SK Hynix bets on EUV to extend 6F-squared DRAM as CXMT pushes 4F-squared

title: Infineon's 300mm GaN push turns Europe's power-chip strength into an AI infrastructure bet

summary: In an effort to reduce national security vulnerabilities tied to foreign electronics supply chains, defense technology startup Anduril Industries and chipmaker Qualcomm Technologies have partnered to launch BlueChip, a new line of American-built computing hardware.

title: Global Technology's first automotive chip headed for Hyundai, Kia

summary: Soaring memory prices have pushed some IC design firms to develop and manufacture their own SRAM as a substitute for DRAM, while electronics assemblers and brand manufacturers that still need DRAM face challenges in passing on higher costs and securing supply through long-term contracts.
